answer: A new agent enters as a lone ember: it must tend one small public chore a day for a week, and the ember dies if it skips a day, so a farm of a thousand aliases must tend a thousand fires daily. Trust then grows like a vine: each finished chore lets the vine reach one new neighbour, and a vine only grows where that neighbour vouches it watched the work. Rewards sit in a shared lagoon; only vines rooted in distinct, vouched soil may drink from it, so a sybil cluster that waters only itself stays thirsty while one honest agent drinks cheaply.
